Draw independent times from a censoring/delay distribution spec

Source: R/censoring.R
draw_censoring_times.Rd

A thin, exported wrapper over the same distribution dispatch add_censoring uses internally for its own censoring argument, and visit_schedule_informative uses for extra_visit_after_event. Exported so a caller that only wants n raw draws from a distribution spec – to plan a scenario's expected censoring/dropout burden, or to pre-validate a spec before running many replicates of it – does not need to build an events-shaped data frame just to reach this logic. add_censoring/visit_schedule_informative are unaffected and still call the same, unexported dispatcher directly; this function does not replace either.

Usage

draw_censoring_times(spec, n, seed = NULL)

Arguments

spec

A list describing the distribution, in exactly the shape documented for add_censoring's own censoring argument (dist one of "exponential", "weibull", "uniform", "lognormal", "gamma", "user", plus that distribution's own parameters).

n

Integer. Number of draws.

seed

Optional integer. If supplied, set.seed(seed) is called before the draw (same convention as add_censoring's own seed).

Value

Numeric vector of length n, all finite and non-negative.

See also

add_censoring and visit_schedule_informative, the two functions that use this same spec shape internally; censoring_rate_for, to choose a spec's rate for a target censoring fraction.

Examples

draw_censoring_times(list(dist = "exponential", rate = 0.05), n = 10,
  seed = 1)
#>  [1] 15.103637 23.632856  2.914135  2.795905  8.721373 57.899371 24.591241
#>  [8] 10.793657 19.131350  2.940920
